clue.text: On appeal, worn out clothing is taken off

indicators.note: clothes wrap around a body, so one piece is dressed around another

blocks.note: SA is short for sex appeal
worn out means exhausted
taken as written

explanation.surface: A worn-out garment is removed during an appeal, as if someone asked for it back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken off' looks like undressing, fitting the clothing theme, but it means mimicked. SA + TIR(IS)ED gives SATIRISED; 'On' simply puts SA first.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to impersonate or mock them for comic effect, which is exactly what lampooning in satire does.

clue.text: Discontented sexy singer kicking leg for playboy

indicators.note: with its contents gone, a word keeps only its outside letters
to kick something is to get rid of it, as in kicking a habit, so letters are dropped

blocks.note: first and last letters of this word
a baritone is a male singing voice
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

explanation.surface: An unhappy, attractive singer is dropped from a show in favour of a playboy.
explanation.walkthrough: ON is removed from BARITONE to leave BARITE, which follows SY. Leg = ON is a cricket convention: the leg side of the field is also the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: A sybarite is someone devoted to luxury and pleasure, a close cousin of the rich hedonist called a playboy.

clue.text: Why Roman chatterboxes assembled their garments?

definitions.text: Why Roman chatterboxes assembled their garments?

blocks.note: surface reading: a riddle asking what reason talkative Romans had for gathering, whose reply would be 'in order to chat'
setter's reading: the loose robes worn by Roman citizens

explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 'why did the chatterboxes gather?' is 'to gas', gas being slang for idle talk; run together, those two words become the Roman robes.
explanation.definitionFit: The toga was the draped woollen outer robe that citizens of ancient Rome wore in public.

clue.text: College employee raised housing rates before half-term, a negative move

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting something turns it bottom to top
a house holds its occupants, so one piece goes inside another
only half of the word is kept, the rest is dropped

blocks.note: a porter keeps the lodge at a college
to rate is to grade
the first half of the word

explanation.surface: A college worker puts up rents just before the half-term break, which is a backward move.
explanation.walkthrough: PORTER turned upwards becomes RETROP, which then houses GRADES followed by TE: RETRO(GRADES TE)P.
explanation.definitionFit: A retrograde step is a change for the worse, a backward movement, so it is a negative or regressive move.

clue.text: Ray's students rejected support

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so its letters run the other way

blocks.note: NUS is the National Union of Students
a beam holds up a structure

explanation.surface: A man called Ray finds his students refusing to back him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray's' reads as possessive, but it is 'Ray is'. The National Union of Students is the UK body representing students, and its initials are the standard crossword 'students'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ray is a single line of light, and a sunbeam is such a line of light coming from the sun.

clue.text: Separate nightclub needing some work internally

indicators.note: something placed internally goes inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: a dive is a seedy bar or club
an erg is a small unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: A standalone nightclub whose interior needs some renovation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Separate' looks like an adjective describing the club, but it is the verb. The erg is a small physics unit of work, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: When roads or opinions separate, they part and go different ways, which is the meaning of the verb in the answer.

clue.text: Sign of damage artist expunged from sacred symbol

indicators.note: to expunge is to strike out, so letters are removed from the word that follows

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist
the scarab beetle was sacred in ancient Egypt

explanation.surface: Someone vandalises a holy emblem, removing an artist's work and leaving a mark of damage.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking RA out of SCARAB leaves SC + AB.
explanation.definitionFit: A scab is the crust that forms over a wound, a visible mark that skin has been hurt.

clue.text: Skedaddle, as one might hope to do at Lord's?

definitions.text: as one might hope to do at Lord's?

blocks.note: first meaning: leave in a hurry

blocks.clueFragment: as one might hope to do at Lord's?
blocks.note: second meaning: a batter plays a cut shot and then scores a run

explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the London cricket ground; a cut is an attacking shot square of the wicket, and a batter who plays one well then hopes to run.
explanation.definitionFit: Skedaddle is informal for making a hasty exit, and to cut and run is the idiom for fleeing abruptly.

clue.text: Rook bitten by monster tit

indicators.note: something bitten sits between the jaws, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: R is the chess abbreviation for rook
a beast is a monster

explanation.surface: Two birds, a rook and a tit, and a monster that bites one of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rook' and 'tit' both look like birds; only the rook stays a bird-shaped abbreviation, while 'tit' is the slang definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tit is a vulgar slang term for a woman's breast, unrelated to the small songbird of the same name.

clue.text: Radioactivity leads to to these first-rate features, written under pressure

blocks.note: alpha, the first Greek letter, means top grade
P is the symbol for pressure
newspaper features are written articles; 'under' places them after the P in a down answer

explanation.surface: A science report praises the first-rate features that radioactivity produces, written up under deadline pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, anything written under a letter comes after it. The printed 'to to' is a typo in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha particles are helium nuclei emitted during radioactive decay, so radioactivity gives rise to them.

clue.text: Great extremes of heat causing depression on the coast

indicators.note: extremes are the two ends, so only the first and last letters are taken

blocks.note: great means big
the end letters of this word

explanation.surface: Intense heatwaves leave coastal people feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' reads as low spirits caused by heat, but it is a physical dip in the coastline.
explanation.definitionFit: A bight is a long curving recess in a shoreline, a wide shallow bay such as the Great Australian Bight.

clue.text: Short work made of new setter's content

indicators.note: the content of something is what is inside it, so only the inner letters count

blocks.note: novel means new
the inside letters of 'setter', leaving off the outer S and R

explanation.surface: A setter says a short piece was made from fresh material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like happiness or subject matter; here it means the inside of 'setter', ETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelette is a short novel or long story, so it is a brief piece of written fiction.

clue.text: Teacher brought back unique meat dish

indicators.note: something brought back returns the way it came, so its letters run backwards

blocks.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir
sole means one and only

explanation.surface: A teacher returns to the canteen for a one-of-a-kind meat course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole' tempts as a fish in a food clue, but here it means only one.
explanation.definitionFit: A rissole is a small fried cake of minced meat, often coated in breadcrumbs, served as a main course.

clue.text: Lady getting round awkward snag puts on show again

indicators.note: turning round faces the other way, so the letters run backwards
something awkward is clumsy and out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: her refers to a lady
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman works her way around a tricky problem before putting an exhibition back up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting round awkward snag' reads as solving a problem; split it, and 'getting round' turns the lady about while 'awkward' jumbles the snag.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallery that hangs pictures a second time displays them again, so to rehang is to exhibit once more.

clue.text: Prime gatherer, in other words?

indicators.note: the same letters expressed as other words means they are rearranged into a new phrase

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone who gathers the best of the crop, put another way.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: rearranged, 'prime gatherer' spells the answer, and read plainly it describes Death reaping people in their prime.
explanation.definitionFit: Death is pictured as a hooded figure with a scythe who harvests lives, a chief collector of souls.

clue.text: European man overtaking me on way to get soap

indicators.note: to overtake is to pass round something, so one piece goes around others

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
a man is a male
taken as written
RD, road, is a way; 'on' puts it after the previous piece

explanation.surface: A European motorist passes the speaker on the road while out shopping for soap.
explanation.walkthrough: Emmerdale is a long-running British TV soap opera set in the Yorkshire Dales. 'Soap' looks like something to wash with; it is a TV serial.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap is a serial drama, and this is one of the longest-running British television soap operas.

clue.text: Disposing of cider and bubbly?

definitions.note: a verbal noun standing for the noun answer

indicators.note: bubbly things fizz and churn, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Pouring away cider and champagne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bubbly' looks like champagne alongside cider, but it signals the rearrangement; 'and' belongs to the fodder, not the surface joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Riddance is the act of getting rid of something unwanted, the noun matching disposing of it.

clue.text: Embracing love, Superman did nothing to change his routine

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so one piece is taken inside the others
a change alters the arrangement, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
taken as written
taken as written
nothing is zero, O

explanation.surface: Superman, smitten, did nothing to alter his daily habits.
explanation.walkthrough: Both love and nothing are zero, O, a tennis and a numeric convention. 'His' ties the definition to Superman's way of working.
explanation.definitionFit: Modus operandi is Latin for method of operating, a person's habitual way of doing things.

clue.text: Green grass on borders of the Blue Grass State rising

indicators.note: lying on the borders of something means surrounding it, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: a sward is a stretch of grassy turf, a green
the Blue Grass State is Kentucky, abbreviated KY

explanation.surface: Fresh grass is growing along the edges of Kentucky, famous for its bluegrass.
explanation.walkthrough: Kentucky is nicknamed the Blue Grass State; KY is its US postal code, and conveniently also its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something going skyward is heading up towards the sky, so it is ascending or climbing upward.

clue.text: One patronised before getting hold of books, say

indicators.note: to get hold of is to grasp, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: pre- means before
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
e.g. means for example, say

explanation.surface: Someone was talked down to before picking up some books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patronised' here means sponsored, not condescended to. 'Say' is the usual crossword signal for an example, EG.
explanation.definitionFit: A protégé is a person who is guided and supported by an influential patron, so is someone given patronage.

clue.text: Correspondence taking a Conservative line

blocks.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a cord is a line or string

explanation.surface: Letters that toe the Tory party line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correspondence' looks like letters, but here it means agreement, as in two accounts corresponding.
explanation.definitionFit: Correspondence can mean agreement or harmony between things, and accord is a synonym for that agreement.

clue.text: Bob's brusque, definitely withdrawn

indicators.note: something withdrawn is pulled back, so its letters run backwards

blocks.note: curt means short and brusque
yes is a definite affirmative

explanation.surface: A man called Bob is curt and, without doubt, reserved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob's' reads as a man's name with a possessive, but it is 'bob is', and a bob is a quick bend of the knees.
explanation.definitionFit: To bob is to make a quick small bow or dip, and a curtsey is the knee-bending bow of respect.

clue.text: Forgot books sent over with German journalist

indicators.note: something sent over another is spread across it on both sides, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
mit is the German word for with
ED, editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: Someone neglected to post the books off together with a German reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With German' asks for the German word for with, not a German person.
explanation.definitionFit: To forget to include something is to leave it out, and omitted means left out or neglected.

clue.text: Typically refrain from extra-large portion

indicators.note: a portion is a piece of something, so the letters are a run taken from within the phrase

blocks.note: a run of letters inside this phrase

explanation.surface: Someone declines a huge helping of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refrain' looks like a verb meaning abstain, beside a big portion; it is the noun, a chorus.
explanation.definitionFit: Tra-la is a nonsense chorus sung in songs, a typical example of a refrain, hence 'typically'.

clue.text: Old section of church rail, generally

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
the nave is the main body of a church
to rail against something is to rage

explanation.surface: An old part of a church's altar rail, typically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rail' looks like a church fitting, the altar rail, but it is the verb meaning to protest angrily.
explanation.definitionFit: Generally and on average both mean as a rule or usually, taking cases as a whole.

clue.text: Master Latin with merit

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for Latin
to merit something is to earn it

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster teaches Latin and passes it with merit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master' reads as a schoolmaster and 'merit' as a grade, but both are verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To master a subject is to acquire full knowledge of it, which is what studying to learn it achieves.

clue.text: Cooks and serves buns?

blocks.note: first meaning: prepares food
second meaning: female rabbits, since bun is a pet name for a rabbit

explanation.walkthrough: Buns look like bread rolls to be baked and served; the question mark flags them as bunnies, and a female rabbit is a doe.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, a person who prepares a meal 'does' it, and female rabbits, like female deer, are called does.

clue.text: Rates of progress back and forth between the stars

indicators.note: going back means travelling the opposite way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: speed is a rate of progress
pace is also a rate of progress

explanation.surface: A spaceship's speeds as it shuttles to and fro among the stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rates' is plural because it supplies two words: one runs back, the other runs forth, as normal.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep space is the vast region of the universe far from Earth, lying out among the stars.
